newsitem.title: GERMANY: German minister wants neo-Nazi ban in army.
newsitem.headline: German minister wants neo-Nazi ban in army.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Friday he wanted recruitment officers to be given more information so that convicted neo-Nazis and racists could be shut out of the army.
His initiative followed two recent brutal attacks by soldiers on foreigners which shocked Germans used to thinking of their army as "citizens in uniform".
"People must not be allowed to lose their trust in our army," Ruehe told the Bild daily newspaper.
He said young men convicted of crimes with racist, extreme right-wing or neo-Nazi motives should not be admitted to the army, a mixture of professionals and conscripts.

"This is not a matter of choosing conscripts according to their personal persuasion, rather of identifying active neo-Nazis and potentially violent thugs in order to protect the Bundeswehr from serious damage," he said.

A Defence Ministry spokesman told a regular government news conference the army currently could not get access to details of crimes committed by juveniles or those with jail sentences under two years when deciding whether to call young men up.

The spokesman said Ruehe wanted the army to be able to see all potential conscripts' criminal records, but that the issue would have to be discussed with other ministries because it had implications for data protection.
Two soldiers, 18 and 20 years old, were detained last Sunday and admitted firebombing a building in Dresden where Italians lived because they hated foreigners.
They were charged with arson and displaying outlawed propaganda materials.
No one was hurt in the blaze, but authorities found swastikas daubed on the building and said witnesses reported that the attackers had shouted Nazi slogans shortly after the fire started.

In March five German soldiers, aged 20 and 21, clubbed two Turks with baseball bats and threatened an Italian with a knife while shouting racist abuse. The soldiers were discharged and given suspended jail sentences.
